summary: The I/II alternation can pair human-group completion with an external agent eliminating that group. English 'were cleansed' in MAC NI .../119 does not make I ṣafən a Detransitive form.
II.3 includes both defeat and lethal elimination. The uncle survives the initial defeat in MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/50; the gloss must not assert killing universally.
The inherited tentative I.2 geraten (???) remains unchanged: 24/266 has source m- plus destination b-. Literal clarity is appended as I.3, not inserted before I.1.
Existing PrS page-style references appear to match PrS 6/7, 68/101 and 71/105; avoid duplicating their quotations or changing numbering systems without collation.

Round 2 only. Jan English is project machine translation, retained verbatim in selected excerpts; semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals are retained as the baseline and are not repeated in this JSON.
Round-1 I.3 clarification of liquid, II.3 opponent elimination, II.4 vineyard depletion and the heart idiom are retained without repetition. Current population-elimination proposals merge into II.3.

mṣafanne in Jan 2.10/2497 has an affair as apparent object amid killing. Jan 2.10/2498 explicitly contrasts survivors, flight and killing. These contexts support II.3 but do not license exact victim counts or killing as the obligatory meaning in every use.
Locative ṣafi with ayko, harke and b-place repeatedly clarifies inherited I.2. No sense is created for each destination.
Is the opponents sense conventional 'ausschalten' or contextual completion? Native judgments should distinguish defeat, killing, depopulation and plundering.
Does MAC NE Interview 2/226 specifically describe killing/removing Zāz's inhabitants or overrunning the place? The proposed gloss leaves the extent open.
In MAC NE Old woman and a fox/35 is complete consumption of grapes intended or more general vineyard damage?
Confirm the segmentation of contracted mṣafanne in 69/465 and whether it is Preterit; retain the reader's provisional box, without adding it as a paradigm example.
Confirm the heart collocation's conventional force: overcoming reservations, consenting, or reconciliation.
Does kəmṣafatte (Jan 2.4/766) mean decipher the written list, get through reading it, or accomplish the task? A distinct reading sense is not established.
Confirm mṣafenalle (Jan 2.22/3995) as singular/plural speaker and patient suffix segmentation; the reconciliation meaning is secure from the quarrel and intervention.
Confirm Preterit-wa ṣafiwo/ṣafənwo and mṣafewole against habitual English; no forms have been rewritten. Does the latter imply forced removal, killing, or both?
Completion extends to a war, a game, a community and a resisting town; contextual death is not encoded by a new Detransitive form.
PrS 51/22 uses a territorial patient for pacifying conflict; retain settlement sense rather than forcing destructive II.3.

Jan repeatedly supports round-1 elimination/defeat; it does not require another exterminate sense. Nominal affair or thing objects in the same violent narrative can be euphemistic, so literal settle is not imposed.
Human-group completion contrasts directly with causative II elimination in Jan 2.10/2498, supporting the round-1 alternation without new Detransitive morphology.
